ledger.summary: Ralph and Roger ride through stony land to a ridge overlooking a wide, empty, grassy valley with a wide river. They swim it rather than use the usual ford downstream, see armed riders spurring toward the water, and gallop over empty downland that Roger says was laid waste by war, ill hap and sorcery. Through an evil-named wood by moonlight they reach at dawn a plain with meadows, tillage and a little river, and a white castle on a green mound, the house from which folk have sought the Well. A gaunt old woman alone serves them and puts Ralph to bed as master.
ledger.geography_notes: Sequence: stony land without rivers but with pools and brooks; a fairly high ridge; a wide well-grassed valley, nearly treeless and uninhabited, with a wide deep slow river (usual ford a mile and a half downstream, the common crossing into the wildwood); a steep hill; empty grassy downland; a wood of evil name ridden all night; an open plain of meadows and fields with a little river and a white castle on a green mound, reached by a ford.
